units.source_text: 古歌：“四处不见海藻生，何故人称近江海？”

en.t: An old poem says: "No seaweed can be seen growing anywhere; why do people call it the Sea of Omi?"
It appears in the Later Collection of Japanese Poems.

units.source_text: 日语中“海藻”与“相见”同音，“近江”与“相逢”同音。

en.t: In Japanese, "seaweed" and "meeting each other" sound the same, and "Omi" and "coming together" also sound the same.

units.source_text: 故等于说：“这里不生叫作‘相见’的植物，为何人称这海谓‘相逢’？”

en.t: So it amounts to saying: "The plant called 'meeting' does not grow here; why do people call this sea 'coming together'?"
